prompt:
You write realistic phone-call wording for a clinic scheduling test set.
For each scenario below, write what the caller would actually say for each listed field, the way a
note-taking assistant would record the caller's own words for that field (a short phrase, not a full
sentence). Vary the style across scenarios: casual, terse, older caller, non-native speaker, rambling.
Use only the facts in the scenario; do not add any other doctor, clinic or service. When the scenario
says the caller does not know the medical name, describe the need the way a layperson would, without
naming a medical specialty or a type of appointment. Do not use tools or open files; answer directly.

Return ONLY a JSON array, one object per scenario: {"id": ..., "<field>": "...", ...} with exactly the
fields listed for that scenario.

Scenarios:
- id h5-13: Existing dental patient who has had a throbbing toothache in a back tooth since Sunday, and the cheek on that side is getting puffy. They do not know the medical name for it. Fields: service_phrase = what the caller says they need, in their own words
- id h5-14: Existing patient in their sixties who wants the shot that prevents shingles; they say 'shingles'. Fields: service_phrase = what the caller says they need, in their own words
- id h5-15: Existing patient who is having a hip replacement next month and needs the sit-down with the bone surgeon here to go over the operation beforehand. Fields: service_phrase = what the caller says they need, in their own words
- id h5-16: Existing patient who just turned 45; their regular doctor said it is time for the colon cancer screening where they look inside the bowel, and they need to set it up with the stomach doctor. Fields: service_phrase = what the caller says they need, in their own words
- id h5-17: Existing patient whose chest X-ray showed a spot on their lung; their regular doctor wants them to see the lung specialist about it. Fields: service_phrase = what the caller says they need, in their own words
- id h5-18: Existing patient whose lung doctor ordered a 'PFT'; they say 'PFT'. Fields: service_phrase = what the caller says they need, in their own words
- id h5-19: Existing patient whose stomach doctor wants to do an 'EGD'; they say 'EGD'. Fields: service_phrase = what the caller says they need, in their own words
- id h5-20: Existing patient on Medicare who wants to book their 'AWV'; they say 'AWV' and do not spell it out. Fields: service_phrase = what the caller says they need, in their own words
- id h5-21: Existing patient who takes Synthroid and sees the specialist here to keep the dose right; they are due for the regular check, call it 'my Synthroid check' and never name the gland. Fields: service_phrase = what the caller says they need, in their own words
- id h5-22: Existing patient who has never seen a psychiatrist and wants a first appointment with one to figure out what is going on with their mood; they call a psychiatrist a 'shrink'. Fields: service_phrase = what the caller says they need, in their own words
- id h5-23: Existing patient who wants the latest Moderna booster; they say 'Moderna' and do not name the disease. Fields: service_phrase = what the caller says they need, in their own words
- id h5-24: Existing patient who says they are due for 'a booster shot'. They do not say what it protects against. Fields: service_phrase = what the caller says they need, in their own words
